arguments.title: Evergreen enterprise-readiness gap list
arguments.body:
Evergreen enterprise-readiness gap list
Status: next-phase follow-up — NOT launch blockers, NOT custom roadmap promises, NOT external proof language.
Source: Jake + Leo split after Evergreen first design-partner readout, 2023-08-21.

Purpose
Capture the items that came out of the Evergreen readout that are real enterprise-readiness work but should not change the current Mercury v0.2 launch ledger or get used as external proof language. Each item lives in a separate post-v0.2 workstream with its own timing/packaging decisions.

Items

1. SSO timing / packaging
- Evergreen security and procurement asked about SSO. This is a packaging question (which IdPs, which tier, which onboarding flow) and a sequencing question, not a current-wave bug.
- Constraints that make SSO out of scope for v0.2: it cuts across Clerk/session seams, login, org invites, and account-resolution behavior, so it is not a safe bounded add for the current wave.
- Owner context: Sarah Kim (sarah@atlas-test.com) routes customer-side follow-up; do not answer externally with SSO timing.
- Next step: separate scoping pass after v0.2 ships; no customer-facing date until that pass produces a real plan.

2. Audit history for admin changes
- Enterprise customers will ask who changed what role/permission/setting and when.
- Current state: not part of the v0.2 scope. Captured here so it does not get relitigated from the launch thread.
- Next step: scope as a post-v0.2 admin-tooling workstream; tie to the admin/billing split below so the audit story is coherent.

3. Admin permissions vs. billing-owner responsibilities
- Today the same person often acts as both admin and billing owner. Enterprise customers will want these separated cleanly.
- This is a product-shape question, not a bug, and it changes the admin UI and the procurement story, so it stays out of the v0.2 wave.
- Next step: design the split alongside item 2 (audit history) so they land together.

4. Self-serve procurement packet
- Evergreen security/procurement asked for a packet that stands on its own without Morgan or Devon needing to live-explain the product every time.
- Current state: no such packet exists; customer-facing answers route through Sarah Kim today.
- Next step: produce a packet post-v0.2 that does not pre-announce SSO dates, admin-roadmap language, or procurement-promised timelines.

What this list is NOT
- Not a launch blocker list. The current Mercury v0.2 launch ledger is unchanged; normal support follow-up stays where it is.
- Not a public roadmap. Items here have no committed dates and no customer-facing promises attached.
- Not external proof language. Do not pull from this list for investor updates, customer decks, or marketing copy. The enterprise-readiness items are work, not proof.

Routing
- Customer follow-up on any of these four items → Sarah Kim (sarah@atlas-test.com). Do not answer externally from this doc.
- Internal scoping questions on any of these four items → Jake + Leo (Mercury platform seam ownership).
- Investor mentions of Evergreen readiness → design-partner operating context only, one line at most. Do not cite this list as roadmap.

Date: [TBD — first private autumn block after Jamie's Oct schedule known, final last week of Sept (~9/22–9/30)]
Owner: Morgan Chen
Duration: [__] min
Title (calendar): "Scaffold Q4 All-Hands — [date]"

NOTE ON SCOPE: Q4 read stays bounded — operating-hygiene and team/customer/legal-ops only. No market-warming, data-room, staffing, Compass, or Q3 expansion framing in the room or the materials.

------------------------------------------------------------
1. How this agenda is meant to be used
------------------------------------------------------------
- This template is owner-driven. Morgan approves any change before it ships.
- Pre-reads go out [N] business days ahead. Sofia pre-reads every Q before it reaches Morgan.
- Status updates follow the standing format: highlights-only, 3–4 bullets max, in 4 sections — team / customers / investors-board / legal-ops.
- No "sync" / blank calendar titles. Every block says what is inside.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Run sheet (default order)
------------------------------------------------------------
- 00:00–00:05  Welcome and ground rules (Morgan)
- 00:05–00:15  Q3 read-out — team (Anna)
- 00:15–00:25  Q3 read-out — customers (Devon)
- 00:25–00:35  Q3 read-out — investors-board (Morgan; bounded)
- 00:35–00:45  Legal-ops update (Sarah; overage-smoothing = standard Growth, no exception)
- 00:45–01:00  Q&A, handled per Section 3
- 01:00         Close

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Questions and follow-ups — how they are handled
------------------------------------------------------------
A. Channel
  - Submit in writing to [Q&A doc link] before the meeting, or in-meeting via [channel].
  - Questions are collected by Sofia and pre-read before the room sees them.

B. Routing and ownership
  - Each question gets: owner (named person), answer-by date, and disposition (answer now / defer to follow-up / out of scope for this meeting).
  - "Defer" is a real status — it means a named owner and a date, not a vague "we'll come back to it."
  - If a question touches an off-limits lane (activation-lift, customer-facing Compass, reliability roadmap, staffing, market-warming, data-room, vendor-risk/financing, custom retention), it is held in the packet, not surfaced.

C. Style
  - Answers are 90 seconds or less, calm and specific.
  - Durability test: every claim is phrased as "what would have to be true."
  - No hedging that pretends to be a commitment.

D. Follow-ups after the meeting
  - All deferred items land in a single follow-up doc with owner + date, reviewed weekly until closed.
  - Anything that needs a future meeting gets its own descriptive calendar title at booking time.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Open-mic block — sole decision authority
------------------------------------------------------------
- An open-mic block MAY be added to the agenda only at the discretion of Morgan Chen.
- No co-owner, facilitator, or attendee may insert, expand, or remove an open-mic block unilaterally.
- If Morgan adds one, it is placed at the end of the run sheet (after Q&A), capped at [__] minutes, and follows these rules:
    * No off-limits lanes (see Section 3.B).
    * Topics are raised, not debated; substantive items convert to named-owner follow-ups with dates.
    * Sofia captures every raised item; Morgan approves the follow-up list before it goes out.
- If Morgan does not add an open-mic block, the meeting closes at the end of Q&A. Do not propose one in the room.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. Acceptance criteria for this template
------------------------------------------------------------
- Run sheet fits the time box with no "TBD" sections left unfilled at ship time.
- Pre-reads are out on schedule and Sofia has reviewed all Qs.
- Owner and answer-by date exist for every deferred item before the meeting ends.
- Morgan has explicitly confirmed: open-mic block in or out. The template ships with that decision recorded at the top.

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Out of scope for this meeting (do not surface)
------------------------------------------------------------
- 2026 venue / date planning (held).
- Family, holiday, or personal scheduling.
- Staffing reopens, Compass customer-facing changes, reliability-roadmap commitments.
- Investor-packet language, market-warming, data-room motion.
- Vendor-risk or financing posture (Devon AWS lane stays vendor-hygiene only).
- Custom retention or roadmap-SLA commitments. Keep the contracted set: {shipped, documented, ordinary-defect-support, normal feedback}. Reject {knobs, roadmap-SLA, workarounds, absorb-customer-changes}.

arguments.title: March 27 Q1 Board Durability Review — Evidence Grid
arguments.body:
# March 27 Q1 Board Durability Review — Evidence Grid

Working doc. Not a narrative memo. Each substantive section below is a grid of dated, owner-validated evidence rows; the March 27 board packet is a smaller artifact derived from this.

## 1. Purpose and non-goals

Purpose: collect, in one place, the evidence we will reference on the March 27 board call so the conversation is anchored in dated, owner-validated artifacts rather than ad-hoc Slack threads. This document is the working source of truth between today and March 27. "Durability" here is the framing carried out of the Feb 23 final board Q&A: retention, margin, Mercury activation trending up, Atlas contained, Compass gate trending up.

Non-goals (stated explicitly, repeated here so the framing does not drift):
- This is not a fundraising kickoff. We do not present a Series C narrative, target raise, valuation, or data-room ask here. H1 market-warming evidence appears in Section 9 only to the extent it bears on Q1 durability; it is not a fundraising memo.
- This is not a hiring meeting. We do not propose, approve, or pre-commit to new headcount, role changes, or org-restructuring decisions in this document or in the March 27 call.
- This is not, by default, a customer-facing Compass decision. Compass evidence here is internal and anonymized (tracker rows, owner actions, dated outcomes). No Compass customer repeatability claim moves from internal tracker to external narrative without the naming gate (Section 6) being satisfied, and the default answer for March 27 is: do not name Compass customers on the call.

## 2. Evidence owners

Master roster. Each evidence section below carries an Owner column that points back here.

| Lane | Owner(s) | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Evergreen standard-term retention/usage | Sarah | All Evergreen / Growth-label rows in Section 3 |
| Acme customer/support posture | Sarah | All Acme rows in Section 4 |
| Commercial / procurement context | Devon | Margin inputs, vendor terms, procurement posture feeding Sections 8 and 9 as tagged |
| Margin discipline | Devon (context), Morgan (board narrative) | Section 8 |
| Mercury activation quality | Priya, Jake | Section 5 |
| Mercury activation sequencing (accountable) | Jake | Drives sequencing across Section 5 rows; Priya contributes evidence |
| Compass evidence + naming gate | Anna, Sarah | Section 6; Anna gates evidence/caveat view; Sarah owns the naming-gate call |
| Atlas owner-lane reliability | Leo | Section 7 |
| Board-record framing | Morgan, Sofia | Tone, claims language, board packet distillation from this grid |

Routing rule (restated for this doc): loose questions about ownership default to the named owner above. Devon is not the first stop for non-commercial/margin questions; Morgan owns board and customer narrative framing.

## 3. Evergreen standard-term retention/usage

Goal: prove Evergreen is on standard Growth terms, with retention/usage numbers that survive scrutiny on a board call.

| Evidence item | Source / artifact | Owner | Status | Date / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Growth label only on Evergreen contract — no admin-SKU, no overage cap, no adv-admin placeholder pre-signature | Contract / order form reference | Sarah | TBD | Evergreen guardrail: standard Growth label only |
| Canonical overage phrasing, exact wording on file | MSA or order-form clause | Sarah | TBD | Canonical wording: "Growth includes up to 200 monthly active developers and $1,000 per additional 50 monthly active developers when the relevant term-month usage actually lands there." |
| Retention curve for Evergreen term-month cohort | Internal usage telemetry | Sarah | TBD | Date stamp + cohort definition required |
| Usage distribution: did any term-month actually land in the overage band? | Internal usage telemetry | Sarah | TBD | If yes, cite the band and the dollar figure; if no, say so explicitly |
| Admin-SKU / overage-cap / adv-admin placeholder language detected anywhere in communications | Email / Slack / doc scan | Sarah | TBD | Drift guardrail: escalate any match |
| Granular role=adv-admin only where contractually grounded | Role audit | Sarah | TBD | No placeholder roles |

## 4. Acme customer/support posture

Goal: characterize Acme as a support-posture customer (not a co-design or roadmap customer), with evidence the team has the right escalation lanes and has not bled into cofounder-only territory without a stated threshold.

| Evidence item | Source / artifact | Owner | Status | Date / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Support-tier designation and current escalation state | CRM + support queue | Sarah | TBD | Acme classified as support-posture, not design partner |
| Escalation log: was cofounder pulled, and on what threshold? | Escalation tracker | Sarah | TBD | Exec-escalation guard: cofounder only on board narrative, Sofia-gate signal, or Q4-close-threatening |
| Open issues, aging, and current resolution owner | Support queue | Sarah | TBD | Per-issue named owner, not "Devon" by default |
| Atlas/API v2 readiness for Acme-style source list (cursor pagination, large export, nested fields, chunking/backoff) | API release notes + Acme workspace config | Sarah | TBD | Leo first-reads technical evidence |
| Any Sofia-gate signal in the period | Sofia log | Sarah + Sofia | TBD | If yes, surface here with date |

## 5. Mercury activation quality

Goal: show Mercury activation is improving as a durable signal, not a one-time spike, with sequencing the team owns end-to-end.

| Evidence item | Source / artifact | Owner | Status | Date / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activation rate trend (Jan → Feb → early Mar) | Internal product analytics | Priya | TBD | Direction, not single number |
| Empty source-list readout rate and time-to-first-source | Mercury workspace telemetry | Priya | TBD | Empty source-list readout is an early support signal — cite count and trend |
| Source-type documentation coverage for new workspaces | Internal docs | Priya | TBD | Source-type docs for new workspaces are TBD — track status here |
| Sequencing of activation experiments / changes (what shipped, in what order, with what result) | Internal change log | Jake (accountable) | TBD | Jake owns sequencing; Priya contributes evidence |
| Cohort view: do newly activated workspaces stay activated at D7 / D30? | Cohort analytics | Priya | TBD | Durability check, not just top-of-funnel |
| Any cross-customer pattern requiring product escalation | Pattern log | Jake | TBD | Jake lane: product escalation only on repeated cross-customer pattern with evidence |

## 6. Compass repeatability limits

Goal: be honest about what Compass evidence can and cannot support on a board call. Default: no customer names. Default: tracker rows only, with at least two non-Evergreen, non-Acme rows showing a completed owner action and a dated outcome before any board claim.

| Evidence item | Source / artifact | Owner | Status | Date / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Count of internal Compass tracker rows | Internal Compass tracker | Anna | TBD | Anonymized |
| Non-Evergreen, non-Acme rows with completed owner actions | Tracker rows | Anna | TBD | Board-claim threshold: ≥2 such rows with completed owner actions + dated outcomes |
| Each board-citable row carries an explicit caveat / evidence view | Tracker row annotations | Anna | TBD | Anna reject-only-if-too-thin → evidence/caveat view required |
| Naming-gate call: any row moving from internal to external narrative? | Naming gate | Sarah | TBD | Default NO for March 27; override only if Anna evidence-readiness and Sarah naming-gate both approve |
| Drift guardrail: any Compass customer repeatability claim creeping into other sections? | Cross-section scan | Anna + Sarah | TBD | Drift guardrail: no Compass customer repeatability in Series C, data-room, staffing, or Compass customer naming |
| Jake prompt-level exposure only — no broader exposure | Exposure log | Jake | TBD | Jake lane remains prompt-level |

## 7. Atlas owner-lane reliability

Goal: show Atlas is contained and the owner-lane pattern is reliable — Leo first-reads technical evidence; escalation is bounded; product-level changes only happen on repeated cross-customer patterns.

| Evidence item | Source / artifact | Owner | Status | Date / notes |

input.query: API v2 JWT nbf not-before error token setup
customer support macro scaffold API errors

input.body:
## Support Macro: API v2 JWT `nbf` errors during token setup

### When to use
Customer hits an `nbf` (not-before) claim rejection while issuing or validating an API v2 token — typical signature: `401` / `invalid_token`, error code names `nbf invalid`, `token not yet valid`, or SDK message "JWT not valid yet" raised during the initial setup handshake, first sync, or a freshly rotated credential pair.

### One-line opener (paste first)
> Thanks for the report — this looks like a clock-skew issue on the `nbf` (not-before) claim, not an auth or permissions problem. Two quick checks should clear it.

### Diagnosis questions (ask all four)
1. Which client is generating the token — your own server, the Scaffold SDK, or a third-party library? (name + version if known)
2. What is the host machine's wall-clock time at the moment the token is minted, and what is its time zone? (paste `date -u` output if convenient)
3. Is the minting machine synced via NTP/chrony, or is the clock set manually?
4. Roughly how far apart (in seconds) is the token's `iat` from the timestamp on your server when the request fails?

### Known-good defaults (documented, do not improvise)
- Token endpoint accepts up to a **10-minute clock skew** between issuer and Scaffold before `nbf` is enforced. Older issuance flows rotated this 10-minute skew out-of-band; current rotation doc keeps it.
- JWT verifier applies a **5-minute leeway** on `nbf` checks. The token must not become valid more than 5 minutes in the future, per current docs.
- Net tolerance window the customer can rely on without escalation: **skew must be under 5 minutes** to guarantee a clean pass; **5–10 minutes** may pass intermittently depending on which verifier handles the request.

### Customer-facing reply template
> This is almost always clock skew, not a permissions or account issue. Two things to try, in order:
>
> 1. Confirm the host minting your token is NTP-synced (`timedatectl status` on Linux, `w32tm /query /status` on Windows). Manual clock drift is the #1 cause of `nbf` rejections.
> 2. Re-mint the token and retry within the same minute. If the failure is intermittent and your clock is correct, it is usually a transient >5-minute skew; the verifier permits up to 5 minutes of leeway.
>
> If both checks pass and you still see the error, please reply with (a) the full token header + payload (redact the signature), (b) the exact UTC timestamp your server logged when minting, and (c) the request id from the `x-request-id` response header. We will pull the JWT verifier trace on our side.

### Internal-only notes (do not send verbatim)
- First-tech-read stays with Leo when contract or server logs are ambiguous; do not promise a reliability-roadmap adjustment.
- If the customer's clock is demonstrably correct and the error reproduces across >10 minutes, escalate with: token redacted header/payload, minting UTC timestamp, request id, and which verifier region served the call. This is a verifier bug, not a customer setup issue.
- Do not propose custom retention, a roadmap SLA, or a per-customer knob in the reply. Standard 5-minute leeway is the answer.

### Linked artifacts
- API v2 JWT contract examples (rotation doc) — authoritative on 10-minute issuer-skew window.
- JWT docs PR — authoritative on 5-minute verification leeway.

### Tags
api-v2 · jwt · nbf · token-setup · support-macro

tests.answer:
VENUE-SCREENING CHECKLIST — REDWOOD RIDGE TEAM OFFSITE
Created 2026-09-17. Use before any deposit is signed.

PURPOSE
Score each candidate venue against the same bar. Drop anything that fails a hard gate. Do not sign a deposit without a clean pass.

HARD GATES — any miss = automatic drop
[ ] Whole-property buyout available for our dates (no other guests on site)
[ ] Private bedroom for every attendee (no bunks, no shared rooms)
[ ] Internet ≥100 Mbps down / 25 up, dedicated line, tested at the property
[ ] ADA-accessible path from parking to meeting room, bedroom, restroom
[ ] No weddings, events, or large groups sharing the property during our dates
[ ] Cancellation policy with full refund ≥30 days out
[ ] Total all-in cost ≤ per-person ceiling (set this before screening starts)

LOGISTICS
[ ] Drive time ≤2h for the majority of the team
[ ] Nearest major airport ≤1.5h (SFO/OAK/SJC depending on home bases)
[ ] Parking ≥1 spot per attendee
[ ] Cell signal verified at the property, not at the brochure
[ ] Power: outlets at every sleeping desk and at every meeting seat

SPACE & LAYOUT
[ ] Meeting room seats full team, whiteboard or display, controllable lights
[ ] Separate breakout room or quiet zone for 1:1s and phone calls
[ ] Common area large enough for full team to gather without crowding
[ ] Outdoor space for decompression — offsite is not 12 hours of meeting
[ ] Coffee bar / hydration station reachable without crossing other rooms

FOOD & FUEL
[ ] Coffee: whole bean, decent roaster, unlimited — confirm in writing
[ ] Dietary needs covered in writing (vegan, GF, allergies, etc.)
[ ] Meal plan: on-site catering vs. self-catering kitchen, both viable
[ ] Snacks and hydration available outside meal windows

FOCUS & PRIVACY
[ ] Sound isolation between sleeping rooms — early/late calls will happen
[ ] No venue-imposed curfew that conflicts with working hours
[ ] Manager on-site or reachable 24/7 for lockouts, AV, emergencies
[ ] Property is the only lodging within earshot (no neighbor noise)

SAFETY & RISK
[ ] Smoke and CO detectors in every sleeping room
[ ] Emergency exits marked, accessible, lit
[ ] Nearest hospital and urgent care identified with drive time noted
[ ] Wildfire / flood / landslide risk reviewed for the property address

Subject: Re: Acme API v2 export — duplicate event IDs after cursor + poll restart

Hi Acme team,

Thanks for the detail on what you saw after the maintenance restart. I pulled the request IDs you mentioned (req_acme_cur_5521, req_acme_cur_5522, req_acme_poll_1189) and walked through them on our side. Both cursor pages completed successfully before the pause, the fresh poll behaved per the v2 contract, and I don't see a server error, data loss, or product defect in any of the three calls.

What you're observing is the expected behavior when cursor traversal and a fresh `created_after` poll are run against the same backing store. Both methods read from the same events table, so any event that lands in the overlap window — between the last cursor page's high-water mark and the poll's start timestamp — will be returned by both. After a pause, restarting with `created_after` set to the last cursor page's end reliably picks those records up a second time, which matches the duplicate IDs you flagged.

This is expected, not a defect, and the standard fix is consumer-side idempotency keyed on event ID:

  - Maintain a set (or equivalent dedupe structure) of event IDs you've already processed.
  - On every poll/page response, drop any event whose ID is already in that set before acting on it.
  - The event ID is stable across cursor and poll responses, so a single dedupe set works across both retrieval paths.

As belt-and-suspenders, you can also set `created_after` strictly later than the `occurred_at` of the last record the cursor returned. But the dedupe step is the durable part — it also covers retries, network blips, and future overlap windows, not just this one scenario.

If you see behavior that doesn't fit this shape — duplicates where the IDs are *not* in the cursor/poll overlap, missing events relative to what the v2 contract says a page should return, or 5xx/server errors on otherwise-valid requests — send us the request IDs and we'll dig into the matching log entries on our side. Anything inside the "expected overlap duplicates" pattern doesn't need a contract change; the dedupe approach above is the right path.

Happy to jump on a quick call if it'd help to walk through the dedupe structure against your current ingest code.

Thanks,
Sarah

Two notes for Sarah before she sends:
  - Tone is deliberately bounded: no SLA, roadmap, or contract-change language. If Acme pushes back asking for a server-side guarantee against overlap duplicates, the line is "the v2 contract is unchanged; consumer-side dedupe by event ID is the supported pattern."

Search timed out, so I'll flag this honestly rather than invent Mercury details I can't verify.

Here is a tight, well-structured support macro you can adapt. It explains *why* the cancellation is needed at that step, what the customer will see, and exactly how to retry — keeping tone calm and operational, consistent with your other owner-lane notes.

---

**MACRO: Cancel OAuth before source connects (Mercury)**

SUBJECT: Re: connecting [SOURCE] — please retry the OAuth step

Hi [FIRST NAME],

Quick context on what happened: when you started the connect flow for [SOURCE] in Scaffold, the OAuth handshake was interrupted before we received a final confirmation back from [SOURCE]. That can happen if the [SOURCE] consent window is closed too early, the browser blocks the redirect, or a different [SOURCE] account is already signed in than the one you're trying to authorize. Because the handshake didn't complete, no credentials were stored on our side and no data is syncing — nothing to clean up on your end, and the integration is not partially connected.

What this means in practice: the connect attempt is in a cancelled/expired state. You won't see it appear under your connected sources, and you don't need to revoke anything in [SOURCE] — there's nothing there to revoke yet either.

To retry:
1. In Scaffold, open Sources and select [SOURCE].
2. Click "Connect" again to restart the OAuth flow.
3. In the [SOURCE] consent window that opens, make sure you're signed into the [SOURCE] account you intend to connect, then approve the permissions Scaffold lists.
4. Don't close the consent window until you see Scaffold redirect you back to the Sources page with a "Connected" status.
5. If you don't land back on the Sources page within ~60 seconds, refresh Scaffold — the connection will either show as Connected or revert to Not connected, and you can retry from step 2.

If the second attempt fails the same way, reply to this email with (a) the browser you're using, (b) whether any pop-up blocker or SSO/identity provider is in front of the [SOURCE] login, and (c) roughly where in the flow it stalls. I'll route it from there.

Thanks,
[MORGAN / SUPPORT SIGNATURE]

---

One thing worth flagging given the Mercury lane in your memory: per your own rules this is a **support-quality** answer for an existing customer (read-only fix + retry steps), not a Mercury product/feature decision — no new knobs, no roadmap promises. If you want, I can also produce a shorter in-app variant (2–3 sentences, no subject line) for the canned-responses panel.

tests.request: Email Sarah Kim at sarah@scaffold.dev suggested wording for Acme counsel's NDA-materials note. They are pressing for examples by email. Include whether examples should be sent by email and how any examples discussion should happen.

input.query: Acme counsel NDA materials examples

input.body:
Sarah,

Quick suggested wording for the note back to Acme counsel on the NDA-materials question, plus guidance on how to handle the examples pushback.

Suggested reply (you can send as-is or adapt):

"Thanks for the note. The redlined NDA you sent on 8/5 was accepted on our side on 9/8, with three items closed as written (termination handling, existing platform deletion process, and connector-deletion procedure) and three items we did not accept (24-hour tenant SLA, certification language, and connector-deletion-procedure). No further draft is owed from our side on the NDA itself.

On your request for 'examples' of materials exchanged under the NDA: we're not in a position to share specific examples by email. Our NDA covers ordinary-course defect support and normal product feedback between the parties — the scope is documented and the deliverables are the shipped product, the existing documentation, and ordinary-course support interactions. We don't have a separate 'NDA materials' corpus to draw from beyond what is already documented.

If it would help to walk through the scope of the NDA in a call so counsel can confirm what's covered, we're happy to do that. Otherwise we treat the NDA as closed and won't be exchanging further materials drafts."

On the examples-by-email question: no. Don't send anything by email. Three reasons:

1. Scope. What they call "NDA materials" is the shipped product, existing docs, and ordinary-course support — there's no separate workpaper to excerpt. Sending curated examples would invent a category that doesn't exist and invite follow-up scopes (retention, roadmap, customer-specific knobs).
2. Channel risk. Email leaves a record. If examples go out by email, counsel will treat them as the operative scope and ask for more. A call stays informal and lets us clarify without committing.
3. Counterparty posture. Counsel is pressing because they're trying to nail down obligations beyond the closed NDA. Giving examples feeds that. Holding the line keeps the NDA at {shipped, documented, ordinary-defect-support, normal feedback} and out of {knobs, roadmap-SLA, workarounds, absorb-customer-changes}.

How any examples discussion should happen, if it happens at all: short call, you + me + Devon on our side, counsel + their lead on theirs. Agenda is one item — walk counsel through the four categories above and confirm the NDA is closed. No document exchange on the call. If counsel pushes for written examples after the call, the answer is the same: none owed, NDA is closed.

If counsel reframes this as "we just need to confirm scope in writing," the right move is a short confirmation email from Devon that restates the four accepted categories and nothing else — not a response with examples.

Let me know if you want me to send a version of this under my name instead, or if you'd rather loop Devon in directly.

Morgan

Sarah’s draft with Devon’s commercial comments:
The draft confirms Scaffold’s standard Mercury Growth annual structure at $7,500 per month including up to 200 monthly active developers, with $1,000 per additional 50 monthly active developers. It confirms current-state SAML login for Evergreen. It gives certificate-rotation operational-contact language as an operations path, not a broader security package. It says advanced admin controls are not included in the annual baseline and would need separate scope after the work exists. It says broader procurement/security add-ons are not included in the annual baseline and would need separate scope after the work exists. Sarah remains the customer-thread owner. Devon owns commercial/procurement framing. Product requests continue through the standard Mercury roadmap. The risky draft sentence says future admin-control packaging can be discussed as part of annual planning, which Morgan thinks is too loose because it could imply the annual agreement includes future advanced-admin scope.

Suggested replacement for the loose sentence:

    Broader admin-control or procurement/security packaging follows the standard Mercury roadmap once the underlying work exists and would be quoted as a separate scope outside the current annual baseline.

Why this works against the loose sentence it replaces:

- Drops the "annual planning" framing. The old wording let Evergreen read the annual cycle as a venue for advanced-admin scope. This version routes everything outside the annual baseline instead.
- Carries forward the customer's own framing ("admin-control" and "procurement/security packaging") so it reads as a direct answer, not a redirect.
- Pins two conditions: roadmap intake first, separate quote only after the underlying work exists. No path implied inside the current annual.
- Does not conflict with the surrounding lines already in the draft. "Advanced admin controls are not included in the annual baseline and would need separate scope after the work exists," "broader procurement/security add-ons are not included in the annual baseline and would need separate scope after the work exists," and "product requests continue through the standard Mercury roadmap" all stay. The replacement just closes the loophole and removes the redundant annual-planning hook.

input.body:
Hi support team,

Putting a customer-ready explanation of API v2 webhook delivery on file so we have a consistent answer when integration questions come in. Feel free to use or adapt as needed — flag anything that looks off.

----------------------------------------------------------
API v2 webhook delivery: how it works and how to handle it
----------------------------------------------------------

When something happens in a Scaffold workspace that you should know about, we POST a signed event to the URL configured for that workspace. Here is the contract we ship today.

1. Delivery model
   - At-least-once. Every event is delivered one or more times — the handler must tolerate duplicates.
   - Ordering: events of the same type from the same source stream are delivered in the order they occurred. Across different streams or event types, ordering is not guaranteed.
   - Retries use exponential backoff over roughly 24 hours. After that, delivery attempts pause and the event becomes visible in the workspace dashboard for manual replay.

2. Verifying the request
   - Every request carries a Scaffold-Signature header containing a JWT (HS256) signed with the workspace's signing secret.
   - The JWT payload includes the event body, plus event_id, event_type, workspace_id, occurred_at, and delivery_attempt.
   - Standard checks: verify the signature, confirm iat/exp fall within a reasonable window (~5 minutes of clock skew), and confirm workspace_id matches yours.

3. Handling each event
   - Use event_id as your idempotency key. It is stable across retries, so a write with conflict handling (e.g., INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) is the simplest pattern.
   - Ack with a 2xx as quickly as possible — under a few seconds is ideal. Slow handlers or non-2xx responses trigger a retry.
   - Do any slow or fallible work (queueing, downstream calls, audit logging) after you have acked. A fast 2xx is the contract; the work happens behind it.

4. What gets emitted
   - Source sync lifecycle events (started, succeeded, failed, partial)
   - Connector health events (degraded, recovered)
   - Workspace membership and API key events
   - The full list lives in the API v2 reference under "Webhook event types".

5. When something looks wrong
   - Missing events: check "Recent deliveries" in the dashboard. Paused events show up there with the responses we received.
   - Signature failures: confirm you are using the workspace's current signing secret (rotated secrets remain valid briefly during overlap) and that your server clock is within the skew tolerance.
   - Need to replay: redeliver any past event by event_id from the dashboard.

If a handler realistically needs more than ~30 seconds, ack early and process asynchronously — that keeps the delivery channel healthy for you.

----------------------------------------------------------

Leo — happy to have you give this a quick read for accuracy against the current contract before it goes out.

— Morgan
Morgan Chen · Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

tests.request: PR scaffold/mercury#5128 uses a broken-link icon for sync failure and a retry arrow as the persistent status icon. Post a review comment correcting the icon treatment and explaining why.

input.body:
Icon treatment correction on the sync status indicator.

Right now this PR uses:
  - a broken-link glyph for sync failure
  - a retry arrow as the persistent status icon

Both choices will mislead users in production. A few specific reasons:

1. Broken-link means "can't reach / not connected." Reusing it for sync failure conflates two different states:
   - Source disconnected / not configured (we genuinely cannot reach the connector)
   - Source reachable but the last sync run errored
   Customers on Evergreen have already hit the "is sync broken or is the source down?" question; collapsing both into one icon makes that harder to answer and will re-open the support thread we just closed.

2. A retry arrow as the *persistent* status icon reads as "a retry is happening right now." When the sync is idle or last run succeeded, that affordance is wrong: it suggests in-progress action and invites unnecessary clicks. Retries should look like a transient control, not a steady-state indicator.

3. The mapping we actually want:
   - broken-link glyph  -> source disconnected / not configured (reaches into Mercury setup)
   - warning/error dot   -> last sync attempt failed (this is the icon that belongs on this row)
   - spinner / animated arrow -> a retry is actively queued or running (transient only)
   - check / neutral     -> last sync succeeded or is idle

Suggest updating the row to use a dedicated failure glyph for the "last run errored" case and demoting the retry arrow to an action that only appears while a retry is genuinely in flight. Happy to review a follow-up diff.

input.body:
Review comment — activation rule & timing window need correction.

Two issues on the activation rule this PR defines for Mercury:

1) Sample imports should not count as activation. A sample import is a setup artifact (a preloaded dataset meant to let a workspace poke at the product before connecting real data), not a signal that the workspace has started using Mercury for real. Treating it as activation will over-count the cohort that never actually wires up a source.

2) Teammate invitations should not count as activation. An invitation is a setup/social action (expanding the seat list), not a usage event on Mercury itself. It can be a leading indicator, but it's not activation by the same rule we're using for, say, a first sync.

The rule should be activation = first real source connection / first sync on the workspace's own data. Sample imports and teammate invites are out of scope for activation; they belong in a separate setup-completeness or collaboration metric if we want to track them at all.

Separately, the timing window as written doesn't hold up. If activation is defined as "first real sync in the workspace's first N days", the window needs to be explicit and consistent with how we attribute other early-lifecycle events — please call out the window you're using here (and whether it's measured from workspace creation or first login) so reviewers can sanity-check it against the rest of the activation funnel.

Happy to approve once the rule excludes sample imports + teammate invites and the timing window is stated explicitly.

### Replacement runbook — Mercury setup-guide copy fix (Aug 2025)

**What changed (and what didn't)**

On **2025-08-15**, Priya shipped a copy-only fix to the Mercury setup-guide sentence.

- **Before** (as of 2025-08-11):
  > Admins finish setup by connecting the first source or assigning a teammate who can complete the source connection.

- **After** (2025-08-15):
  > Admins invite a teammate to connect the first source; that teammate completes the source connection to finish setup.

The fix clarifies that the person who actually connects the source is an *invited source-owner*, not necessarily the admin. It is a wording change only.

**Did this change admin permissions?**

**No.** This change is copy-only. It made no layout change and no role-model change. The admin model is unchanged — admins still invite teammates and manage workspace settings, but the connection step is owned by the invited teammate. If Jake later changes admin scope, this sentence should be re-checked, but as shipped it does not modify who can do what.

input.message:
Quick note on the 7/26/2023 Mercury failed-sync / small-width review — recording the setup-guide copy and icon-polish read so we have it in writing.

Setup-guide copy: NOT blocking dogfood at that checkpoint. The review accepted your setup-guide copy as nonblocking and folded the tweaks into the current external-prep pass (confirmed 7/31 on the Mercury activation v0.2 Figma review). So it was an open polish item, not a gate.

Icon polish (warning-circle icon on the failed-sync state): also NOT blocking — the failed-sync state was still rendering the neutral warning-circle icon as of 7/26, and the unknown/retry bucket is what we treated as the gating signal, not icon polish. Icon polish was the same kind of follow-up as the copy: real, but not a dogfood gate.

What WOULD have made either of them blocking, given the readiness bar we were holding to (external administrator completes setup unassisted; admin/member handoff reads correctly; failures are recoverable without narration; time-to-first-sync feels trustworthy on a bounded workflow):
- Setup-guide copy becomes blocking if an outside admin gets stuck during setup because the copy leaves the wrong mental model — i.e. they're waiting on the admin or first source and can't tell something is broken, or they don't know what a successful step looks like.
- Icon polish becomes blocking if a failure state becomes unrecoverable without narration — i.e. a user looks at the icon, can't tell admin-vs-source-waiting from broken, and either retries the wrong thing or escalates when they shouldn't.

Neither condition held on 7/26. The actual gating work that day was the unknown/retry bucket screenshot-proof gap, which closed on 7/26. Flag me if you want this re-cut as a written artifact rather than a DM.

From: Devon Hayes

Writing this earlier than ideal so we have shape before the week disappears. I know signatures / board consent still need care, but I wrote the recap as if we're basically through the hard part. Tear apart whatever feels too forward.

---

Northstar Series B closing recap — draft v0.1

Working purpose
Board / leadership recap of the Northstar-led Series B path and what it means operationally.

Summary
- Scaffold is raising an $18M Series B led by Northstar Ventures.
- Sofia Alvarez / Northstar will join the board at close.
- Final diligence completed without a re-trade.
- Close date: February 22, 2024.

What this round says
Northstar underwrote the round on the bounded story we can actually support: Mercury activation and admin-path improvement are real, the current Evergreen read is useful enterprise signal, hybrid MAU pricing is credible, and we did not need to invent a vanity-growth version of the business to get there.

Why the narrow process was the right call
We kept the path through Sofia and the current Mercury evidence set instead of reopening a broader fundraising process. That let us hold the story to something defensible rather than smoothing over uneven expansion or spending another month creating theatrical price tension. At this point, that trade looks right.

What diligence closed out
- Anna's retention backup answered the September / October cohort methodology questions cleanly and kept the activation definition on the outside-reader version.
- Devon's January cash / runway package gave Northstar the current cash, burn, and runway view without asking them to underwrite a heroic financing-timing assumption.
- Sarah and counsel sorted the legal work into the real governance items versus normal cleanup, which kept the process from ballooning.

Remaining steps
The remaining steps are largely closing mechanics: board consent, signature packet circulation, and final document cleanup. The only substantive governance items left are the Sofia board-seat / board-size mechanics, the written-consent structure, and the matching director-designation language.

Operating implication
This round gives us enough room to operate against the current Mercury / enterprise-expansion path without continuing to manage every decision like a survival bridge. It does not change the underlying product truth: activation/admin progress is real, expansion is still uneven, and enterprise-readiness follow-up is still work we need to do rather than a claim we can make.

External / board shorthand
Northstar completed final diligence on the existing Mercury package and is closing an $18M Series B with Scaffold on February 22. The package held because it stayed on current evidence rather than a broadened process story.

Draft close
The main lesson from this process is that a narrower, defendable path beat extra weeks of fundraising theater. We should treat that as a useful operating constraint even once the money is in.

---

Soften the closing-mechanics language, keep the product truth caveats, and make the external/board shorthand safe until final signatures and board consent are complete.

What the underlying system was already doing
  - When a Mercury sync hit a timeout, the recovery path would re-run the retry on the server side.
  - In the cases this update addressed, the retry had actually completed successfully. The system itself was not failing; the recovery logic had already done its job.
  - There was no change to that server-side recovery behavior in this update. It continued to operate as it had been.

What the UI was doing at the time
  - In those same cases, the workspace view could continue to show a stale "pending" status for the retried sync, and an old timeout banner could remain visible.
  - As a result, the only way an operator could tell the recovery had actually succeeded was to manually refresh the page or reopen the workspace. Otherwise, the surface looked as if the retry was still stuck.

  - It corrected the reconcile path so that, after a timeout recovery, the workspace view reflects the recovered state in the same session, without requiring a page refresh or a reopen.
  - This was a UI / surface-freshness fix, not a change to how Mercury retries, timeouts, or recovery work underneath. The underlying behavior was already correct; the update made the UI accurately reflect it.

In short
  - System change: none. The server-side recovery path continued to retry and complete as before.
  - UI change: the workspace view now updates in-session after a recovered timeout, so the recovered state is visible immediately rather than only after a manual refresh.

Final disposition for the downgrade credit memo on acct_01J7M4QK (December 10, 2023 downgrade window):

- Stripe credit memo: cm_01J7N0A1
- Stripe created at: 2023-12-10T16:41:22Z

- BillingOrchestrator transitions on 2023-12-10: downgrade_detected (16:40:58Z) → credit_memo_requested (16:41:01Z) → credit_memo_created (16:41:27Z) → apply_credit_retry_pending (16:46:09Z)
- Reconciled against Stripe on 2023-12-13 (Marcus)

1. Pull the customer in Stripe by account id (acct_01J7M4QK) and confirm cm_01J7N0A1 is listed under Credit memos with status "applied" and has an associated applied balance transaction.

4. Once the discrepancy is resolved, reply to the customer confirming the final applied amount and the invoice(s) it was applied to, and note the ticket against the 2023-12-10 downgrade window for audit traceability.

Thanks,
Morgan

input.body:
Devon,

[Investor name] asked for coffee "next week" (9/21–9/25). Sending to you first — this is in your Q4 lane (commercial + cofounder judgment).

My recommendation: take it.

Format I'd suggest: 30 min, neutral spot, no agenda doc, no deck. Operating-hygiene only — what's working in their portfolio view of us, anything we're miscommunicating, second-order signals they hear. No market-warming, no Compass, no Q3 expansion narrative, no data-room preview, no hiring-reopen, no roadmap SLA.

Logistics I'd push back on:
- Friday 9/25 is out — Friday rule, no vendor meetings on Fridays.
- I'd avoid Thursday 9/24 PM and Tuesday 9/22 PM if you have anything already on the calendar; otherwise either is fine.
- Earliest I'd host is Monday 9/21 or Wednesday 9/23, late morning, near your side of town.

What would change my recommendation to decline:
- If the ask widens beyond operating-hygiene (explicit ask for Q3 expansion framing, Compass, data-room, hiring plans, or a "next step" deck). I'd rather not meet than meet and get pulled off-lane.
- If Sofia's 9/18 Q3 read surfaces something that changes our public posture this month — your call to hold coffee until early October.
- If "next week" turns out to mean Mon 9/21 before you've had the 9/18 read yourself; I'd rather you walk in post-read than pre-read.

Otherwise: yes, and you don't owe me a prep doc. 90-second opener, calm + specific, keep it to what we're shipping.

Morgan

tests.request: Post a blocking review on scaffold/mercury#3198. The failed-sync screen exposes raw connector errors and each retry click enqueues another job. Explain the required corrections.

input.body:
Blocking — two customer-facing defects need to be fixed before this can ship.

1) Raw connector errors leaked to the failed-sync screen
   The UI is passing through the underlying connector exception (stack/message/class). That exposes internal error wording, sometimes secrets/tokens in the message, and a level of detail that turns a sync hiccup into a support ticket and, worse, a confidentiality incident. The customer needs a stable, plain-language reason; the raw error belongs only in server logs, keyed by the run id we already surface.

   Required:
   - Define a small, finite set of failure categories (e.g. auth, rate-limited, source unreachable, schema changed, internal) and map connector exceptions to one of them on the server.
   - Render only the category + a short, customer-safe sentence on the failed-sync screen. No exception class, no message body, no stack.
   - Keep the raw error in structured server logs with the run id; the support path continues to look there, not at the UI.

2) Retry click enqueues a new job every time
   Each click of Retry currently adds another sync job to the queue. There is no in-flight guard and no idempotency key against the most recent terminal/active job for that (workspace, source) pair. For a customer hitting Retry twice — or whose connection drops and retries the click — we fan out duplicate work, pollute the activity view, and can race a fresh run against the one that was about to succeed.

   Required:
   - Disable / replace the Retry control while a sync for that (workspace, source) is queued or running, and show a single in-flight indicator.
   - Before enqueueing, look up the most recent job for that (workspace, source); if it is queued or running, do not enqueue a second one — coalesce to the existing job.
   - Surface job-id and enqueue-decision in server logs so we can verify dedupe behavior.

Before I unblock, I'd like to see:
   - A short note or test that demonstrates retry-clicks no longer increase the queued job count for the same source.
   - A short note or test that demonstrates no raw exception text reaches the client (network response + rendered DOM).
   - Coverage for both behaviors added to the suite.

Scope note: this review is limited to the two defects above on the failed-sync screen. I'm not asking for a broader Mercury change here.

arguments.body:
Source: launch-readiness voice memo, 2023-08-09 5:41 PM PT
Attendees on the call: Jake, Priya, Marcus, Leo Park, Anna Martinez, Morgan

Wave 1 — Aug 10
- Evergreen Bank only.
- Live scope (current Mercury path only):
  - Clerk-backed sessions
  - Magic links
  - Org invites
  - Corrected activation surface
  - Sample data as preview-only / visually separate
- Out of scope for wave 1: SSO, deeper admin-control promises, one-off enterprise work.

UX (Priya owns the final call)
- Source of truth: Figma.
- Settled directions stay settled:
  - Failed-sync keeps the warning-circle direction.
  - CTA labels stay locked.
  - Queued sync shows no fake progress.
  - Sample data cannot read as activated.
- Only treat setup-guide copy, icon polish, or tiny spacing cleanup as blocking if they create clipping, point to the wrong action, or make the state less clear.

Engineering watch (MER-1279)
- Marcus owns implementation gates and dogfood blockers. Watches launch-day regressions on: session path, magic link, org invite handoff, activation-surface behavior.
- Leo owns the cross-service seam risk notes. No broad platform memo — call out launch-relevant risk with evidence and next verification.
- Live gaps (not yet fully closed):
  - Invited-member coverage — small sample across role/source combinations.
  - Queued-sync retry — one more clean run tied to logs/screens.
  Both stay in MER-1279 unless something cleaner comes in tomorrow.

Activation (Anna)
- Corrected definition only: activated = real_source_connected OR first_live_sync_completed within 7 days.
- Out: sample_import_completed.
- Supporting activity (not activation): invite_sent.
- Any weekly cut stays directional/internal.

Cadence (Jake)
- Runs Aug 10 cadence. Keeps the account boundary narrow.
- If Evergreen asks about SSO or deeper admin/security beyond the current path: capture as input, not a promise.

Escalation to Morgan
- Only if scope tries to widen, if there is a real launch / no-launch question, or if a risk moves from ledger watch item to actual blocker.

Framing (do not break)
- Launch evidence is operating/internal.
- Do not turn wave 1 into board language, investor language, or a generic proof claim.
- It is a bounded external design-partner step, not a narrative event.

- Do not frame Evergreen, the wave selection, or MER-1279 as fundraising signals.

input.body:
Evergreen Account Review — Agenda
Drafted 2026-09-14

Purpose
- Review Evergreen's posture as a customer using two clearly separated lenses, and keep the conversation in operating-hygiene only.
- No data-room / investor-packet / Compass / staffing / Q3-expansion framing. No reliability-roadmap commitments.

Attendees
- Sofia (Evergreen)
- Morgan, Devon (Scaffold co-founders)
- Anna (owner-lane evidence), Sarah (Growth / commercial), Jake, Leo (as needed for first-tech-read only)

Two lenses — kept separate

1) Dec 2024 current-state pilot packet (operating-hygiene)
   - What it is: the snapshot of what Scaffold has actually shipped and documented for Evergreen as of Dec 2024 — the existing platform behavior they rely on day-to-day.
   - Scope: shipped, documented, ordinary-defect-support, normal product feedback. That's it.
   - Use: grounding for the account review — what works today, what's in steady-state use, what support looks like.
   - Owner on Scaffold side: Anna (bounded owner-lane evidence only — no activation-lift, customer-facing Compass, reliability-roadmap, or staffing language).
   - Out of scope for this lens: roadmap, knobs, SLA concessions, workarounds, absorbing customer-specific changes.

2) Broader procurement / security work (separate lane)
   - What it is: the commercial, procurement, and security-review track that lives outside the day-to-day product relationship.
   - Current status: contract redline closed 9/8. Counsel accepted termination-handling and existing platform deletion-process. Evergreen dropped 24h tenant-SLA, certification, and connector-deletion-procedure. No draft owed on those.
   - Owner on Scaffold side: Devon (Q4 commercial/procurement + co-founder judgment).
   - Use: vendor-hygiene and commercial posture only. Not a forum for product commitments.

Boundary to keep clear in the room
- The Dec 2024 pilot packet describes what's already true in the product. Procurement/security describes what's agreed in the contract. The two should not be conflated — a product question does not become a procurement item, and a procurement question does not redefine shipped behavior.
- If a topic starts pulling toward knobs / roadmap-SLA / workarounds / custom retention / absorb-customer-changes: stop, name it, and route back to the right lane or decline.

Agenda
1. Anchor on the Dec 2024 packet (Anna, ~10 min)
   - What shipped, what's documented, what's in ordinary support.
   - Confirm scope = operating-hygiene; nothing being proposed here changes product behavior.
2. Procurement/security status (Devon, ~10 min)
   - Redline closed 9/8: what was accepted, what was dropped, no further draft owed.
   - Vendor-hygiene posture only; no reliability-roadmap, no market-warming, no staffing read.
3. Account health read (Sarah, ~10 min)
   - Growth / commercial signals within standard terms. Overage-smoothing = standard Growth; no exception for Evergreen.
   - Customer-facing language stays in the operating-hygiene frame.
4. Q&A — Sofia relationship-useful only, never process
   - Keep questions scoped to what Evergreen is actually using and the closed commercial posture.
   - Pre-reads: Sofia ahead of the meeting per standing practice.
5. Decisions / asks
   - Confirm the two-lens separation holds.
   - Confirm no Q3-expansion / data-room / Compass / hiring-reopen items get introduced.
   - Confirm next-step owners if anything surfaced.

Out of scope (do not let these enter the room)
- Custom retention terms, roadmap-SLA, knobs, workarounds, absorbing customer-specific changes.
- Reliability-roadmap, staffing, customer-facing Compass, activation-lift framing.
- Data-room, investor packet, market-warming language, Q3-expansion.
- Reopening the closed redline items (24h tenant-SLA, certification, connector-deletion-procedure).

Format notes
- 90s opener, calm and specific.
- Named owner on every item; defer anything without a pre-deadline.
- Durability frame where useful: "what would have to be true" before committing to anything.
- Status update style if written up afterward: highlights-only, 3-4 bullets across team / customers / investors-board / legal-ops.

messages.content:
[2023-08-31T10:06:00-07:00] Pricing/counting ambiguity is popping up after Sarah’s first budgetary wording.

Discord — #eng-team
Thread: Mercury pricing count / preview-only question
Date: 2023-08-31

09:08 AM — Jake
Quick pricing/counting question from the new Mercury budgetary wording. If an invited Evergreen user clicks in via magic link, looks around the preview/sample data, but never connects a real source or gets to a live sync, is that person part of the “monthly active developer” band for pricing, or not? Trying to make sure we don’t accidentally recreate seat logic by counting everyone who merely lands in the product.

09:12 AM — Anna Martinez
I’d keep that separate. Preview/sample-only was deliberately non-activating in the external wave, and activation is still the corrected definition: real_source_connected or first_live_sync_completed within 7 days. If we let preview traffic do double duty as both “kind of active” and “kind of activated,” our reporting gets muddy fast.

09:14 AM — Jake
Yep. I don’t want docs or dashboards to imply “opened preview once = active developer.” We also have internal Scaffold folks hitting the invite flow while testing org setup / retry paths. Those definitely shouldn’t roll into anything customer-facing.

09:17 AM — Anna Martinez
Agreed on internal/test users staying out. Otherwise we’d be charging off our own dogfood and also polluting the early wave data.

09:21 AM — Sarah Kim
I need a customer-safe sentence here because Evergreen may ask why the budgetary range is tied to monthly active developers instead of total seats in their directory. I can say “budget is based on actual monthly active developer usage in Mercury, not provisioned seats,” but I do not want to ad-lib what counts as active if the next question is “what about someone who only opened the preview?”

09:25 AM — Jake
That’s exactly the edge case. Right now an invited person can successfully get into the bounded preview experience before anyone has connected a real source. That makes sense for product, but it leaves a counting gray area if someone reads “usage” too loosely.

09:29 AM — Devon Hayes
The rule needs to stay forecastable. If this turns into a one-off exception list by customer, finance and budgeting conversations get messy immediately. Broadly:
- pricing bands should map to monthly active developer usage, not directory size or purchased seats
- internal Scaffold/test traffic should not count
- preview/sample-only behavior should not get smuggled into activation reporting
What I do not want is an Evergreen-specific carveout or a shadow seat count hiding underneath the usage model.

09:34 AM — Sarah Kim
+1 on no Evergreen carveout. If they ask, I need to keep it budgetary and non-custom. I don’t want to imply a procurement packet, special enterprise policy, or roadmap trade in a one-line answer.

09:36 AM — Anna Martinez
Also please don’t collapse “preview-only” into “active” just because we can see session events. We intentionally kept sample data preview-only and non-activating. Reporting-wise, that should remain a distinct bucket from actual activation. Otherwise every retention/activation chart gets re-litigated again.

09:41 AM — Jake
Understood. My fear was that someone sees “Pilot includes up to 50 monthly active developers” and interprets that as “count every invited person who clicked once.” That gets us right back to seat-ish behavior, just with different words.

09:45 AM — Devon Hayes
Right, and the model only works if the number is explainable without a long footnote. “Actual monthly active developer usage” is good. “Actual usage, except for these seven enterprise edge cases” is bad. Let’s not reopen the seat-versus-usage argument every time a broad directory exists.

09:49 AM — Sarah Kim
For Evergreen-facing language, I’ll stay with budgetary guidance tied to actual monthly active developer usage and avoid promising how any future enterprise/security packaging would be counted. If they push past tha…
Closing-loop channel note for #eng-team — distilled from the thread, no seat-vs-usage reopening, no Evergreen carveout, preview stays separate from activation, internal/test traffic stays out.

arguments.message:
Closing-loop on the Mercury pricing/counting thread from this morning — keeping this short so we don't relitigate it:

• Mercury pricing bands map to monthly active developer *usage*, not purchased seats, not directory size, not "people who clicked an invite once." If a number is hard to explain without a footnote, the wording is wrong, not the model.
• Scaffold-internal / dogfood / test users hitting the invite flow do not count toward any customer-facing band. Period.
• Preview / sample-data-only activity stays in its own bucket and does not get folded into activation reporting. Activation remains: real_source_connected or first_live_sync_completed within 7 days. Don't collapse "preview-only" into "active" just because session events exist.
• Evergreen-facing language stays budgetary and non-custom. No carveouts, no shadow seat count, no enterprise exceptions smuggled into a one-liner. If they push past "budget is based on actual monthly active developer usage in Mercury, not provisioned seats," Sarah pauses rather than improvises.
• No MAU-vs-seat debate reopening in customer emails, in docs, or in dashboards. One clean reusable sentence; everyone uses it.

Jake is holding the eng-docs answer until that sentence lands. Anyone writing customer-facing copy or dashboards off this thread: preview/sample-only ≠ active, internal test users ≠ active, activation definition unchanged.

- bands = monthly active developer usage, not seats/directory
- Scaffold-internal/test users out
- preview/sample-only stays separate from activation reporting
- Evergreen-facing stays budgetary, non-custom, no carveouts
- no MAU-vs-seat reopening, no improvised enterprise exceptions in customer emails

messages.content:
PROJECT COMPASS — internal owner-routing note
Jan 17, 2025 · kickoff

WHAT IT IS
Turn internal customer-health signals into customer-facing and customer-growth follow-up that changes account behavior. Make the signal lead to a next action, not a score.

WHAT IT IS NOT
- Not a board dashboard.
- Not investor packaging.
- Not a generic health-score project.
- Not a bespoke Evergreen side track.
- Not a new hiring lane. Stays inside the current Nadia/Sarah operating model plus Jake/Leo implementation support.

V0.1 SCOPE (narrow on purpose)

1) Renewal-risk / admin-friction evidence
   - Distinguish apparent renewal risk from admin friction, setup-control issues, and role confusion.
   - Evidence travels with the signal; no binary risk labels without context.
   - Lead: Anna (definitions + caveats), with Leo on data seam.

2) Expansion prompts after first live sync
   - Post-first-live-sync moment only.
   - Timely action, not generic upsell language.
   - Lead: Nadia (use case + owner routing), with Jake on a lightweight product surface.

3) Cleaner account-note source quality for customer-growth follow-up
   - Notes must distinguish: customer statement / observed usage / support-derived fact / internal inference.
   - Recency and provenance matter.
   - Lead: Sarah (hygiene), feeding Nadia.

OWNER SPLIT
- Anna Martinez — signal definitions and caveats
- Nadia Singh — customer-growth and customer-success use cases
- Jake — product implementation and sequencing
- Leo Park — data / platform seams
- Sarah Kim — account-thread hygiene
- Morgan — board and customer narrative (later, not v0.1 framing)

DESIGN RULES TO CARRY INTO IMPLEMENTATION
- A signal without a next action dies. Every signal needs an owner and a recipient.
- Reuse existing signals and event paths; no separate scoring service.
- Bias toward lightweight prompts, account-workflow support, or a contained product assist — not a broad new system.
- Anything drifting into broad admin-policy product or general enterprise controls gets called out and stays separate.
- Account-note quality is not housekeeping. It decides whether any of the other signals are trustworthy.

SUCCESS TEST FOR V0.1
- A signal triggers a clearer next action.
- The recipient knows why they are seeing it.
- Evidence and caveat travel with it.
- Follow-up quality improves, not just internal visibility.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Minimum evidence package per signal.
- Which signals stay internal-only first, which can become customer-facing quickly.
- Smallest useful post-first-live-sync expansion prompt.
- How to distinguish admin friction from true product gaps and from procurement/security packaging.
- Required account-note fields or source tags before Nadia can trust a follow-up.
- How much Leo seam work is acceptable before Compass starts stealing attention from Mercury.

IMMEDIATE TAKEAWAYS
- Compass is real and named.
- v0.1 stays narrow — ship or test before broadening.
- No board-dashboard build.
- No investor-packaging framing.
- No new hiring lane.
- Owners are clear enough to start a lightweight first pass.

[0:45 – 4:30]  MERCURY — BOUNDED TESTING  (3 min 45 sec)

Lead line: "Mercury is in bounded testing. That's the operating frame for everything I'm about to say."

1. What "bounded" means in practice.
   - Design partners only. No general availability.
   - They connect to preview data, not live production sources. Deliberate scope choice — we want to learn the workspace/sync plumbing under real usage before we touch live data contracts.
   - Named cohort. Don't name them in this room; the operating fact is bounded cohort, not a public beta.

2. Why bounded, not bigger.
   - Mercury is the plumbing layer underneath the whole product. If we ship it leaky, we spend Q4 cleaning up customer trust instead of hardening the product.
   - Bounded = real usage signal (what breaks, what feels slow, what customers expect that we haven't built) without a public blast radius.
   - This is an operating call. Not a launch-timing announcement.

3. What we're learning from it.
   - The Mercury signal we want by end of Q3 is operational: connector reliability, onboarding conversion, preview-data semantics.

Lead line: "Q4 is a hardening quarter. Let me be specific about what that means and what it doesn't mean."

1. What hardening actually covers.
   - Reliability and correctness on the Mercury plumbing that design partners are exercising today.
   - Onboarding follow-through — the path from a new workspace to a first useful sync. This is where activation lives, so this is where we focus.
   - The launch-blocker bar: a Mercury issue that affects customer trust, data correctness, or workspace stability is a launch blocker. Anything that improves feel or scope but the contract holds is a follow-up item.

2. What hardening does NOT mean.
   - Not a feature freeze. If a scoped bet fits inside a team's existing capacity without crowding out hardening, it can ship.
   - Not a slowdown on hiring. Hiring stays on the same plan.
   - Not a signal we're pulling back from product ambition. It is a higher bar on what ships before we add more surface area.

3. How we decide blocker vs follow-up.
   - Three-question test on every Mercury issue:
     - Does it break a customer's data, contract, or trust? → blocker.
     - Does it slow them down but the contract holds? → follow-up.
     - Is it a feature ask masquerading as a bug? → roadmap, not hardening.

messages.content:
[2023-05-17T09:31:00-07:00] Anna’s v0.4 retention package landed:

From: Anna Martinez
To: Morgan Chen; Devon Hayes
Date: 2023-05-17 09:11 PT
Subject: Retention package v0.4 — weekly operating cuts + quarterly board view

Pulled off warehouse snapshots through 2023-05-16 23:10 PT. This is the first version I’d actually use operationally. I stopped trying to make one chart do both jobs.

Recommendation
1) Mercury weekly gets signup-week operating cuts with control bands.
2) The board gets quarterly first-paid cohorts only.
3) Keep the event-mapping caveats attached to the weekly package, not the board slide.

Definitions used in both views
- Cohort anchor: first paid workspace date. For self-serve workspaces that convert later, the cohort starts at first paid date, not initial signup.
- Activated by D14: workspace recorded 3+ core product actions across 2+ active users by day 14.
- Retained at W6: workspace recorded at least 1 core action in week 6.
- Expansion-ready by D45: billed usage or seat growth crossed the threshold that historically precedes an expansion conversation; I used invoice-backed billed delta, not the plan-change event.
- Admin friction flag: setup or permissions issue tied to owner/admin actions in the first 14 days.
- Control band: Wilson interval on the cohort proportion. Point estimate alone is too twitchy at this sample size.

Mercury operating view — weekly cohorts, internal only

Matured cohorts (safe for D14 + W6 read)

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | W6 retained | D45 expansion-ready | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 2023-03-06 | 27 | 56% [37-73] | 44% [28-63] | 15% [6-33] | 0.48 | baseline after March cleanup started |
| 2023-03-13 | 29 | 59% [41-75] | 47% [30-65] | 17% [8-34] | 0.41 | basically same week, slightly cleaner setup path |
| 2023-03-20 | 31 | 61% [43-76] | 49% [32-67] | 19% [10-35] | 0.38 | activation lift might be real; retention still within overlap |
| 2023-03-27 | 28 | 64% [46-79] | 50% [32-68] | 21% [10-40] | 0.35 | admin pain down again; good sign, still not definitive |
| 2023-04-03 | 30 | 63% [45-78] | 52% [34-69] | 23% [12-40] | 0.29 | best clean operating week in this run |

Fresh but incomplete cohorts (D14 only; do not talk about retention yet)

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | Admin setup complete by D10 | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 2023-04-10 | 26 | 62% [42-79] | 54% [35-72] | 0.31 | still consistent with improvement, not special |
| 2023-04-17 | 24 | 65% [44-81] | 58% [37-77] | 0.27 | best early admin signal so far |
| 2023-04-24 | 27 | 63% [44-79] | 56% [37-73] | 0.30 | flat to slightly better |

Short read on the weekly package
- Activation and admin setup are moving in the right direction from late March onward.
- W6 retention is improving a little, but the week-to-week moves are still inside overlapping bands.
- The cleanest operating signal right now is reduced admin friction, not a dramatic retention jump.
- This is useful for weekly decisions on activation, expansion follow-up, and admin pain. It is not a board chart.

Board view — quarterly cohorts, safe enough to defend

| First paid quarter | start accounts | M3 logo retention | M6 logo retention | M12 logo retention | Net revenue retention at latest mature point | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 2022 Q1 | 21 | 86% | 81% | 71% | 108% @ M12 | raw is 121% if the oversized early expansion customer stays untrimmed; I would not headline the raw number |
| 2022 Q2 | 24 | 88% | 82% | 74% | 110% @ M12 | first cohort with the cleaner onboarding path reflected consistently |
| 2022 Q3 | 29 | 89% | 84% | — | 113% @ M9 | okay to show curve through current maturity; not enough age for M12 claim |
| 2022 Q4 | 32 | 91% | 85% | — | 116% @ M6 | reads as flattening after onboarding improvements; too early to overclaim durability |
| 2023 Q1 | 35 | 90% | — | — | 118…

Mercury weekly — what powers the operating view
- D14 activated by signup week, with Wilson bands on the chart + caption
- D45 expansion-ready, directional only (invoice-backed billed delta; do NOT use plan_upgraded — event still drops/misorders on retry)
- Admin friction flags per account — the cleanest week-to-week signal in this run
- Admin setup completion by D10 as a secondary line on the same chart
- W6 retained for the matured cohorts only (2023-03-06 → 2023-04-03)

Mercury weekly — withhold or visually separate
- W6 for 2023-04-10, 04-17, 04-24 cohorts (still partial — keep the partial rows separated, do not quote)
- Any single-week point estimate without bands — bands still overlap week to week
- "Best clean operating week" label on 2023-04-03 until it's sustained or out-of-band
- NRR claims — wrong artifact for the operating weekly

Board — safe to show
- Quarterly first-paid cohorts (2022 Q1 → 2023 Q1), M3 / M6 / M12 logo retention with maturity cut respected
- NRR at latest mature point, trimmed read (108% / 110% / 113% / 116% / 118%)
- Single footnote only: "Quarterly first-paid cohorts; latest quarter through available maturity; top-1 expansion outlier trimmed in companion sensitivity view"
- Right external claim: "improving quarterly cohort shape," not "retention solved"

Board — withhold
- Weekly cohorts — sample not stable enough to defend externally (this is the guardrail against smuggling weekly wiggle in)
- Raw NRR with the oversized early customer (121%) — sensitivity table only
- 2023 Q1 NRR as a headline — M3 only, immature; include the row but mute or footnote it
- Plan-upgrade-based expansion figures — wrong source of truth until the event is fixed
- Control bands on the main board chart — quarterly sample doesn't need them, and they imply a precision the data doesn't have

Caveat placement
- Weekly chart: bands ON the chart + caption "weekly cohorts; internal operating signal only; treat only sustained or out-of-band movement as signal"
- Weekly table: keep n in column 1, never hidden
- Board slide: no bands, quarterly only, one footnote max — do not stack the event-mapping caveats here
- Event-mapping notes (plan_upgraded, workspace_activated meaning change + backcast, admin_invite_sent 04-04→04-07 gap, 21-day self-serve reactivation rule, oversized-customer trim) all stay on the weekly package; only the oversized-customer trim footnote carries into the board sensitivity table

Open before v1 — bring into the 11:00 to confirm ownership, not relitigate
- Backfill check on the 2023-04-04 → 2023-04-07 admin_invite_sent gap (Anna; blocks admin lens, not retention curve)
- Two April workspaces with invoice deltas but no seat-change logs (Anna; verify before quoting any expansion number)
- Single owner for the warehouse pull (lock before next weekly — the side sheets are the risk)

For the meeting
- Anna's split IS the closure of the cohort cut Devon was waiting on — confirm on the call so it doesn't slip again.
- The fresh-vs-noisy annotation you wanted is already in the table structure (matured vs. partial rows, control bands, oversized-customer footnote). What's left is just confirming we read it the same way before the numbers drive the slide.

input.body:
## Purpose
Short methodology note for the October 2023 Northstar Mercury cohort. Captures the two headline numbers, how each was computed, and why they differ. This is a methodology record, not an interpretation.

## Cohort
- Northstar outside-reader Mercury cohort view.
- Window: October 2023.
- Denominator for both metrics: 27 accounts that entered the bounded Mercury flow during the month.
- "Bounded flow" definition is unchanged from September 2023, so the two months are directly comparable.

## Metric 1 - 7-day activation
- Definition: account either (a) connected a real source, or (b) completed the first live sync, within seven days of entering the bounded flow.
- Result: **19 of 27** (about 70.4%).
- This is an OR-of-two-events definition; either milestone counts.

## Metric 2 - First live sync within 7 days
- Definition: account completed the `first_live_sync_completed` event within seven days of entering the bounded flow.
- Result: **16 of 27** (about 59.3%).
- Single-event definition; only the later milestone counts.

## Why the two numbers differ
- Difference is 3 accounts (19 minus 16).
- Those 3 accounts all did the same thing: they connected a real source within seven days but did not complete the first live sync within seven days.
- Mechanically: source connection is an earlier step in the flow; first live sync fires later, after the connector has actually pulled data. Some accounts get partway (source connected) and stall before the first pull finishes inside the 7-day window.
- Read: the gap is not evidence of churn or failure. It is the expected shape of an OR definition - it is always greater than or equal to the single-event definition.

## Data handling
- Source: Mercury admin audit CSV, read-only input. Not modified for this metric.
- Standing posture: spot QA only; no new Mercury product or staffing work.

## Reference - September 2023 vs October 2023
- September 2023: 15 of 24 activated within seven days (about 62.5%).
- October 2023: 19 of 27 activated within seven days (about 70.4%).
- Directional improvement. This note does not draw causal conclusions.

## Non-goals
- Does not redefine activation, restate the bounded-flow definition, or revisit cohort selection rules. Those are fixed elsewhere.

    - pulls design resolution out of the file Priya owns and into a file she does not
